back: 1. Single Field Index: Indexes created on a single field of a document. Example: Creating an index on the name field.

back: Indexes allow MongoDB to quickly locate and retrieve the required documents, reducing the need for full collection scans.

front: What is MongoDB connection in one sentence?
back: URI + driver options that keep your app talking to the right cluster under load and failover — MongoDB Manual + production incident patterns.

front: Explain the mental model of MongoDB connection (how the system thinks).
back: The driver maintains a connection pool to mongod/mongos processes. Each URI encodes auth, replica set name, TLS, and read/write preference. On startup the driver discovers topology (standalone → replica set → sharded). Writes go to the primary (unless you explicitly use secondary reads with caveats); reads follow readPreference.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for MongoDB connection?
back: App → Driver pool → Primary (writes)

front: What is MongoDB errors in one sentence?
back: Symptom → cause → fix for the errors that show up in prod logs and Compass — MongoDB Manual + Mongoose gotchas.

front: Explain the mental model of MongoDB errors (how the system thinks).
back: MongoDB errors fall into a few buckets: wire/auth (can't connect), write concern / topology (not primary, election), schema/validation (document shape), index/constraints (duplicate key), and query/update syntax (wrong operator shape). The message usually names the bucket; the fix is in the operator or topology state.

back: Mongoose updateOne without $set — { name: "x" } replaces entire doc in some paths; use $set explicitly for partial updates. front: When should you NOT use MongoDB errors?
back: Don't blanket catch and retry without reading error code — duplicate key and validation errors won't heal on retry. Don't disable write concern globally to "fix" timeout errors.

back: Schema + indexes + hooks that define document shape, constraints, and query paths — Mongoose docs + DBA review habits.

front: Explain the mental model of MongoDB model (Mongoose schema) (how the system thinks).
back: A model is a compiled schema bound to a collection. The schema declares fields, types, defaults, validators, indexes, and middleware. MongoDB is schemaless at storage time; Mongoose enforces structure at the application layer unless you bypass it with strict: false or raw collection calls.

front: What is MongoDB replica set in one sentence?
back: Primary + secondaries + oplog for durability and automatic failover — MongoDB Manual (Kleppmann-style distributed ops).

front: Explain the mental model of MongoDB replica set (how the system thinks).
back: A replica set is a group of mongod processes that replicate the same data. One primary accepts writes; secondaries pull from the primary's oplog (capped collection of operations). Arbiters vote in elections but hold no data. Members heartbeat each other; primary loss triggers election (~seconds).

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for MongoDB replica set?
back: Client writes → Primary → oplog → Secondaries (async lag possible) → Arbiter (vote only)

front: Given a broken MongoDB replica set setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Client writes → Primary → oplog

front: Symptom: No primary / RECOVERING — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: rs.status() · Fix: Fix network; restore member; re-sync secondary

front: Symptom: High replication lag — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: rs.printSlaveReplicationInfo() · Fix: Scale primary load; disk I/O; index hot writes

front: Symptom: Rollback after failover — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Logs "rollback" · Fix: Re-sync affected secondary from backup

front: Symptom: Split-brain (two primaries) — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: rs.conf() priorities, votes · Fix: Odd number of voting members; fix network partition

front: Symptom: Writes fail during election — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Brief window · Fix: Retry with backoff; tune serverSelectionTimeoutMS

front: Symptom: Arbiter-only RS (even count) — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Design review · Fix: Prefer 3 data-bearing nodes; arbiter is cost hack with risk

front: Gotcha with MongoDB replica set: what silently fails?
back: Read from secondary without secondaryOk — driver defaults to primary for consistency. Write concern { w: 1 } only — ack from primary ≠ replicated; data loss if primary dies before replicate. Hidden/delayed secondaries — good for DR/analytics; don't point prod reads at delayed node.

front: When should you NOT use MongoDB replica set?
back: Don't run production on standalone mongod — no failover, no oplog backup story. Don't use arbiters as a substitute for a third data node when you care about durability.

front: What is Mongoose plugin in one sentence?
back: Reusable schema functions that add paths, indexes, methods, or hooks without copy-paste — Mongoose plugins docs.

front: Explain the mental model of Mongoose plugin (how the system thinks).
back: A plugin is a function (schema, options) => void registered on a schema before mongoose.model(). Global plugins apply to every schema. Plugins compose: one adds soft-delete, another adds pagination, another adds audit fields.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Mongoose plugin?
back: plugin(schema) → adds paths / hooks / statics → schema.plugin(plugin, opts) → per-schema → mongoose.plugin(plugin) → global (all schemas)

front: Symptom: Plugin hook never runs — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Order of plugin() vs model() · Fix: Register plugin before mongoose.model()

front: Symptom: Global plugin breaks one schema — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: schema.plugin override · Fix: Disable per-schema or guard with option flag

front: Symptom: Duplicate index from plugin — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: schema.indexes() · Fix: Merge indexes; one plugin owns index

front: Symptom: Method not on document — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Applied to wrong schema · Fix: Confirm schema.plugin on correct schema

front: Gotcha with Mongoose plugin: what silently fails?
back: Plugin order matters — pre-hooks run in registration order; conflicting plugins need explicit ordering. Global plugins in tests — leak across test files; call mongoose.deleteModel() / isolate connections. Over-plugining — magic behavior hides in hooks; hard to debug "who filtered this query?".

front: When should you NOT use Mongoose plugin?
back: Don't plugin one-off business logic — plain schema methods or service layer is clearer. Don't global-plugin heavy side effects (external API calls) without opt-in per schema.

front: Explain the mental model of Mongoose middleware (how the system thinks).
back: Middleware runs between Mongoose API call and MongoDB operation. Hooks attach to save, validate, remove, and **find* query methods** — not all methods trigger all hook types.

front: Symptom: Infinite loop — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: Hook didn't run — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: this is wrong in arrow fn — what do you check and fix?

front: Gotcha with Mongoose middleware: what silently fails?

front: When should you NOT use Mongoose middleware?
back: Authorization / tenancy — enforce at API/gateway layer; query middleware is defense-in-depth only. Cross-collection invariants — use transaction + explicit domain service, not cascading hooks. Heavy I/O in pre hooks — blocks request; queue async job in post-commit hook or outbox pattern.
